_comment: Enzyme activity registry. enzymes: genotype_activity is the clearance multiplier for that phenotype relative to a normal metaboliser, back-derived where possible from the AUC ratio of a sensitive substrate that is named in the note; phenotype_frequency is European. perpetrators: residual enzyme activity is NOT stored - it is derived at load time from index_auc_ratio and the index substrate's own index_fm, as residual = (1/ratio - (1 - fm)) / fm, and checked against the FDA class band. Reading a residual straight off the AUC ratio would overstate the remaining activity. CAVEAT: every index substrate here (desipramine, omeprazole, tizanidine, midazolam) was dosed ORALLY, so the ratios include gut-wall inhibition and loss of first-pass extraction and residuals derived from them overstate the purely hepatic effect - most for CYP3A4. A second caveat for genotype_activity: it is applied to one pathway, but several values were read off whole-drug exposure ratios without an fm correction; see each note. verified=true: the value was checked against the primary document named in source - an SPC or regulator label, the original study's full text (or its abstract, where the note says 'abstract only'), or a registry's posted results - and the note says where. verified=false: no primary could be reached, primaries disagree, or a field is calibrated rather than observed; the note says which. Drug-information aggregators and label mirrors are never a source for a verified value (tests/test_data_provenance.py).

CYP2D6.note: Not verifiable as a single number. Strattera label: atomoxetine AUC about 10-fold higher in poor metabolisers (1/10 = 0.10); its PK table, corrected for bioavailability (63 % vs 94 %), gives a clearance ratio of 0.128. Ultrarapid: the nortriptyline gene-copy series (Dalen 1998) implies about 1.33. Intermediate is the CPIC activity score 0.5, not a measured ratio. CAVEAT: the multiplier is applied to one pathway but derived from whole-drug ratios without an fm correction. Frequencies: phenotypic PM 7.0 % (Sachse 1997, 589 Germans); genotype-predicted European PM 5.44 % (Gaedigk 2017). Risperidone is deliberately not the anchor: its active moiety is CYP2D6-independent.

CYP2C19.note: Not verifiable as stated. Poor: oral omeprazole AUC ratios (7.5-fold, Klotz) are confounded by bioavailability; the IV arm of PMID 17203292 gives clearance multipliers of 0.23 (PM) and 0.58 (heterozygous EM). Ultrarapid 2.1 is exact (Baldwin 2008: *17/*17 omeprazole AUC 1973 vs 4151). The '12-fold' figure could not be traced. Poor-metaboliser frequency 0.03: Prilosec label, 'approximately 3% of Caucasians'. CPIC does not use activity scores for CYP2C19.

CYP2C9.note: Celebrex label: celecoxib systemic levels 3- to 7-fold higher in *3/*3 than in a pooled *1/*1 or *1/*3 group, so 0.14-0.33 and, against *1/*1 alone, lower. CPIC NSAID guideline: *3/*3 ratio of means 4.16. Intermediate 0.5 lumps *1/*2 (no effect) with *1/*3 (x1.62). No preset uses a CYP2C9 pathway.

CYP3A4.note: No poor/intermediate/ultrarapid system exists for CYP3A4, so there is no genotype selector - only inhibition and induction. 'normal' = 1.0 is the loader's normalisation, not a datum. The cited table is from a CYP3A4*22/tacrolimus meta-analysis and does not address phenotype classes. CYP3A5 expresser status is a separate axis not modelled here. Enzyme turnover half-life 36 h (kdeg 0.0193 /h, Fan et al. PMC6310869, Simcyp default) governs the onset of induction.

CYP1A2.note: No validated genotype-based activity multiplier; the *1F effect appears only alongside an inducer such as smoking (KNMP/DPWG background text, a guideline rather than a primary), so no genotype selector is offered.

perpetrators.name: Paroxetine 20 mg/day
perpetrators.note: Laine 2004 (abstract): paroxetine 20 mg/day for 8 days, single 100 mg desipramine, n=15, AUC x4.8. Index substrate desipramine, fm 0.85 = 1 - 15/102 from median clearances in poor vs extensive metabolisers (Brøsen 1993, abstract); this assumes no residual activity in poor metabolisers, whereas enzymes.json gives them 0.12, which would make fm about 0.97. Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss. PK: PAXIL FDA label: mean elimination half-life ~21 h; once daily.

perpetrators.name: Fluoxetine 20 mg/day
perpetrators.note: Preskorn 1994 (abstract): fluoxetine 20 mg/day, desipramine 50 mg/day at steady state, 18 healthy extensive metabolisers, AUC0-24 x4.8. The previously cited review table has no numbers. Index substrate desipramine, fm 0.85 = 1 - 15/102 from median clearances in poor vs extensive metabolisers (Brøsen 1993, abstract); this assumes no residual activity in poor metabolisers, whereas enzymes.json gives them 0.12, which would make fm about 0.97. Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss. PK: Prozac FDA label: parent chronic half-life 4-6 days (120 h). Offset is longer: the active metabolite norfluoxetine has a 8.6-9.3 day half-life, so a single half-life understates how slowly CYP2D6 inhibition fades.

perpetrators.name: Bupropion
perpetrators.note: Wellbutrin SR label: bupropion 150 mg b.i.d. with a single 50 mg desipramine, AUC 'approximately' 5-fold; the effect persists at least 7 days after the last dose. Index substrate desipramine, fm 0.85 = 1 - 15/102 from median clearances in poor vs extensive metabolisers (Brøsen 1993, abstract); this assumes no residual activity in poor metabolisers, whereas enzymes.json gives them 0.12, which would make fm about 0.97. Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss. PK: Wellbutrin SR label: mean elimination half-life 21 h; 150 mg b.i.d. Hydroxybupropion also contributes, so inhibition persists several days after stopping.

perpetrators.name: Terbinafine
perpetrators.note: Lamisil label 7.1: desipramine AUC 5-fold (Madani 2002: 482 -> 2383 ng*h/mL, x4.94, terbinafine 250 mg/day for 21 days); still present at the last observation 4 weeks after stopping. Index substrate desipramine, fm 0.85 = 1 - 15/102 from median clearances in poor vs extensive metabolisers (Brøsen 1993, abstract); this assumes no residual activity in poor metabolisers, whereas enzymes.json gives them 0.12, which would make fm about 0.97. Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss. PK: LAMISIL FDA label: effective half-life ~36 h governs plasma decline; a 200-400 h tissue terminal phase explains the ~4-week persistence of CYP2D6 inhibition, which a single half-life understates. Once daily.

perpetrators.name: Fluvoxamine 50 mg/day
perpetrators.note: Yasui-Furukori 2004 (Br J Clin Pharmacol 57:487) Table 1: fluvoxamine 25 mg b.i.d. (50 mg/day, not 100-150) for 6 days, single 40 mg omeprazole, homozygous extensive metabolisers, AUC ratio of geometric means 8340/1483 = 5.62 (the text's 6.2-fold is a mean of individual ratios). Inhibition is dose-dependent. Index substrate omeprazole: fm 0.85 is not established by any primary; the primaries bracket it at 0.84-0.90 (1 - 1/6.29 = 0.84 from Kang 2002; 0.87-0.90 from Yasui-Furukori's poor vs homozygous extensive metabolisers). Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss. PK: Fluvoxamine maleate FDA label: steady-state half-life 15.6 h; 50 mg once daily.

perpetrators.name: Fluconazole
perpetrators.note: Kang 2002 (abstract): fluconazole 100 mg/day for 4 days, omeprazole 20 mg, n=18 healthy men, AUC0-inf 491 -> 3090 ng*h/mL (x6.29). Diflucan label: strong CYP2C19, moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor; this entry covers CYP2C19 only. Index substrate omeprazole: fm 0.85 is not established by any primary; the primaries bracket it at 0.84-0.90 (1 - 1/6.29 = 0.84 from Kang 2002; 0.87-0.90 from Yasui-Furukori's poor vs homozygous extensive metabolisers). Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss. PK: DIFLUCAN FDA label: terminal half-life ~30 h (range 20-50); once daily.

perpetrators.name: Ciprofloxacin
perpetrators.note: Zanaflex label and Granfors 2004 (abstract): ciprofloxacin 500 mg b.i.d. for 3 days, single 4 mg tizanidine, n=10, AUC 10-fold (FDA index table: 9.74). FDA classes ciprofloxacin as a moderate CYP1A2 inhibitor that can act as a strong one with highly sensitive substrates such as tizanidine. Index substrate tizanidine, fm 0.97 = 1 - 1/33, a lower bound from the fluvoxamine study. Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss. PK: CIPRO FDA label: serum elimination half-life ~4 h; every 12 h.

perpetrators.name: Fluvoxamine
perpetrators.note: Zanaflex label and Granfors 2004 (abstract): fluvoxamine 100 mg once daily for 4 days, single 4 mg tizanidine, n=10, AUC 33-fold (range 14-103; FDA index table: 32.73). Index substrate tizanidine, fm 0.97 = 1 - 1/33, a lower bound from the fluvoxamine study. Orally dosed, so the ratio includes first-pass loss. PK: Fluvoxamine maleate FDA label: steady-state half-life 15.6 h; the CYP1A2 (tizanidine) regimen was 100 mg once daily.

perpetrators.name: Ketoconazole 200 mg b.i.d.
perpetrators.note: FDA index-substrate table: oral midazolam AUC ratio 15.90 with ketoconazole (Olkkola 1994: 400 mg once daily for 4 days, n=9; midazolam syrup label +1490 %). Tsunoda 1999 gave 16-fold with 200 mg doses, the regimen in this entry's name (same daily dose). Index substrate midazolam (oral): fm 0.96 is uncited, and the published static-model value is 0.91-0.92 (Loue & Tod 2014, from Ohno 2007), so not verified. Oral ratios include gut-wall CYP3A4, so residuals derived from them overstate the hepatic effect on drugs whose fm is hepatic. PK: Ketoconazole tablets label: biphasic elimination, terminal half-life 8 h; the DDI-study regimen was 200 mg b.i.d.

perpetrators.name: Clarithromycin
perpetrators.note: Primaries disagree on the same study (Gorski 1998, clarithromycin 500 mg b.i.d. for 7 days): the clarithromycin label gives oral midazolam AUC +600 % (x7.0), FDA's index-inhibitor table x9.61, and Quinney 2008 restates x8.1 (its elderly cohort: x8.0). The stored 8.4 matches none exactly. Index substrate midazolam (oral): fm 0.96 is uncited, and the published static-model value is 0.91-0.92 (Loue & Tod 2014, from Ohno 2007), so not verified. Oral ratios include gut-wall CYP3A4, so residuals derived from them overstate the hepatic effect on drugs whose fm is hepatic. PK: Clarithromycin label: half-life 5-7 h at 500 mg; every 12 h. Also a mechanism-based inhibitor, so offset lags its own clearance.

perpetrators.name: Diltiazem
perpetrators.note: Midazolam syrup label Table 2 and Backman 1994 (abstract): diltiazem 60 mg t.i.d. for 2 days, oral midazolam 15 mg, n=9, AUC +275 % (45/12 = 3.75); FDA class moderate. Index substrate midazolam (oral): fm 0.96 is uncited, and the published static-model value is 0.91-0.92 (Loue & Tod 2014, from Ohno 2007), so not verified. Oral ratios include gut-wall CYP3A4, so residuals derived from them overstate the hepatic effect on drugs whose fm is hepatic. PK: Diltiazem HCl immediate-release label: elimination half-life ~3-4.5 h; the interaction study used 60 mg t.i.d. (every 8 h).

perpetrators.name: Carbamazepine 400 mg b.i.d.
perpetrators.note: Kanefendt 2024 (abstract only): carbamazepine 300 mg b.i.d. for 10 days after titration (this name says 400 mg b.i.d., the regimen of the paired mirtazapine study), healthy volunteers, midazolam AUC ratio 0.282 (second study 0.323). In chronically treated patients the midazolam label gives -94 % (x0.06). Induction takes at least 2 weeks to build and to wane (Czech risperidone SPC 4.5). Index substrate midazolam (oral): fm 0.96 is uncited, and the published static-model value is 0.91-0.92 (Loue & Tod 2014, from Ohno 2007), so not verified. Oral ratios include gut-wall CYP3A4, so residuals derived from them overstate the hepatic effect on drugs whose fm is hepatic. PK: TEGRETOL FDA label: autoinduced steady-state half-life 12-17 h (14 h); b.i.d. Induction onset is set by enzyme turnover, not this value.

perpetrators.name: Rifampicin
perpetrators.note: Midazolam syrup label Table 3: rifampin 600 mg/day, oral midazolam AUC -96 % (x0.04; Backman 1996: 0.42/10.2 = 0.041, n=10, during dosing). Replaces 0.18, which no primary reports; the previous source was a PBPK simulation. FDA's index table gives 0.016 with midazolam one day after the last dose (Backman 1998). Because oral midazolam carries gut-wall induction, the hepatic effect derived from 0.04 is large: see the derived diazepam estimate against its SPC (clearance about 4x). Index substrate midazolam (oral): fm 0.96 is uncited, and the published static-model value is 0.91-0.92 (Loue & Tod 2014, from Ohno 2007), so not verified. Oral ratios include gut-wall CYP3A4, so residuals derived from them overstate the hepatic effect on drugs whose fm is hepatic. PK: RIFADIN FDA label: half-life ~3 h (2-3 h repeated); 600 mg once daily. Induction onset is set by enzyme turnover.
